name: Canada
description: Canada from the Norse at L'Anse aux Meadows and New France to Confederation, two world wars and a constitution of its own.

checkpoints.name: Vikings and New France
checkpoints.note: Norse sailors camped at L'Anse aux Meadows about the year 1000. Centuries later Cartier sailed up the St Lawrence, Champlain founded Quebec, and the Hudson's Bay Company traded furs across the north.

checkpoints.name: British North America
checkpoints.note: Britain won New France on the Plains of Abraham. Its colonies held off American invasion in the War of 1812, and the Franklin expedition vanished searching for the Northwest Passage.

checkpoints.name: Confederation and the west
checkpoints.note: Four colonies joined as Canada in 1867 under John A. Macdonald. Louis Riel led the Métis in two risings, the railway reached the Pacific, and gold drew thousands to the Klondike.

checkpoints.name: War and a nation of its own
checkpoints.note: Canadians took Vimy Ridge, Toronto gave the world insulin, and the Statute of Westminster gave Canada its own laws. The Maple Leaf flag, Expo 67 and the constitution of 1982 followed, then the Vancouver Olympics and Justin Trudeau and Mark Carney as prime ministers.
